question: In the traditional accounts of Vijayanagara, who were referred to to as narapati or "lord of men"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rayas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• In the context of the Vijayanagara Empire, the term **"narapati"**, which translates to "lord of men," was used to refer to the **Rayas**, the rulers of the empire.

• The Vijayanagara Empire, established in 1336, was primarily ruled by dynasties like the Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu. The kings of these dynasties were referred to as Rayas.

• The Rayas were considered the supreme authority in the empire, holding political, military, and religious leadership.
